subject: AcreetionOS Update — June 29, 2026
body:
Recent updates to our continuous integration pipeline have significantly improved the reliability of our ISO build process, with changes such as per-pipeline staging directories to avoid publish races between concurrent builds, and the use of relative symlinks for the latest.iso file, ensuring it resolves correctly on the host web root. These tweaks may seem minor, but they have a major impact on the overall stability of our release process, which you can track on our changelog page at https://acreetionos.org/changelog.html.

Development
Our team has been busy refining the inner workings of AcreetionOS, with a focus on maintaining the integrity of our Arch-based foundation, including keeping up with the latest security updates, such as those issued for AlmaLinux, and ensuring our kernel is always up-to-date, like the recent 7.1.10 and 6.18.46 stable kernel releases. For more information on how we manage our system's security and updates, you can visit our documentation at https://acreetionos.org/docs.html.

Community
The broader Linux community has also seen some exciting developments, including the release of Emacs 31.1, which brings a host of new features and improvements to this venerable editor. If you're interested in learning more about how to get the most out of Emacs on AcreetionOS, be sure to check out our wiki at https://acreetionos.org/wiki.html, where you'll find guides and tips on everything from installation to customization. And for the latest news and updates, you can always visit our flash page at https://acreetionos.org/flash.html.
